title: Forgiveness is the fast that makes one fearless
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 223
summary: The shabad begins by naming forgiveness, good conduct, and contentment as the real fast. It moves through release from disease and death-fear and settles in the Lord already present within and without.
whyItMatters: This is for the person holding hurt so tightly that it has started feeling like identity. Held faithfully, it turns forgiveness from sentiment into discipline and lets fear lose some of its hidden power.
takeaway: Forgiveness, conduct, and contentment free the heart from fear.

lines.translation: Gauree, First Mehla:
To practice forgiveness is the true fast, good conduct and contentment.

lines.gurmukhi: ਰੋਗੁ ਨ ਬਿਆਪੈ ਨਾ ਜਮ ਦੋਖੰ ॥
lines.transliteration: rog na biaapai naa jam dhokha(n) ||
lines.translation: Disease does not afflict me, nor does the pain of death.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮੁਕਤ ਭਏ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਰੂਪ ਨ ਰੇਖੰ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: mukat bhe prabh roop na rekha(n) ||1||
lines.translation: I am liberated, and absorbed into God, who has no form or feature. ||1||
What fear does the Yogi have?

lines.gurmukhi: ਰੂਖਿ ਬਿਰਖਿ ਗ੍ਰਿਹਿ ਬਾਹਰਿ ਸੋਇ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: rookh birakh gireh baahar soi ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: The Lord is among the trees and the plants, within the household and outside as well. ||1||Pause||
The Yogis meditate on the Fearless, Immaculate Lord.
Night and day, they remain awake and aware, embracing love for the True Lord.
Those Yogis are pleasing to my mind. ||2||
The trap of death is burnt by the Fire of God.
Old age, death and pride are conquered.
They swim across, and save their ancestors as well. ||3||
Those who serve the True Guru are the Yogis.

lines.gurmukhi: ਭੈ ਰਚਿ ਰਹੈ ਸੁ ਨਿਰਭਉ ਹੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: bhai rach rahai su nirabhau hoi ||
lines.translation: Those who remain immersed in the Fear of God become fearless.
They become just like the One they serve. ||4||
The Name makes a man pure and fearless.
It makes the masterless become the master of all. I am a sacrifice to him.
Such a person is not reincarnated again; he sings the Glories of God. ||5||
Inwardly and outwardly, he knows the One Lord;
through the Word of the Guru's Shabad, he realizes himself.
He bears the Banner and Insignia of the True Shabad in the Lord's Court. ||6||

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਬਦਿ ਮਰੈ ਤਿਸੁ ਨਿਜ ਘਰਿ ਵਾਸਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: sabadh marai tis nij ghar vaasaa ||
lines.translation: One who dies in the Shabad abides in his own home within.
He does not come or go in reincarnation, and his hopes are subdued.
Through the Word of the Guru's Shabad, his heart-lotus blossoms forth. ||7||
Whoever is seen, is driven by hope and despair,
by sexual desire, anger, corruption, hunger and thirst.
O Nanak, those detached recluses who meet the Lord are so very rare. ||8||7||

structure: It opens by redefining austerity through forgiveness and character instead of display.
The middle loosens disease, death-fear, and the authority of threat itself.
It ends in the Lord's nearness within and without, where fear has less room to stand.
